provenance: First derived TWICE, independently, by two agents that saw no implementation (none existed) and did not see each other, and committed BEFORE any verdict code was written, per REQ-04 as strengthened by the kickoff attack panel. CORRECTED 2026-09-19 (face v2 Phase 05 PR 3a logic attack): both derivations, and the code written against them, paired Newcombe's terms for p1 - p2 while the test is on d = p2 - p1, so every lower bound with unequal arms was too high -- 0.0661 on Newcombe (1998)'s own worked example, whose published value is 0.0524. Two derivations that share a misreading agree with each other and prove nothing. The `independent_*` values are now EXACT: tests/fixtures/evolve/newcombe-exact.mjs computes each case in 120-digit fixed-point arithmetic with no code shared with verdict.mjs, rounds once to the nearest double, and refuses to run unless it reproduces the published example.
form_note: centre = (2np + z^2) / (2(n + z^2)); halfw = z*sqrt(z^2 + 4np(1-p)) / (2(n + z^2)). z^2 is z*z, never a literal. The half-width uses 4*n*p*(1-p), NOT 4*x*(n-x)/n. p-l and u-p are literal subtractions, never replaced by halfw. l and u are clamped into [0,1] AFTER the roots are computed. Every one of those rules changes the last bits if broken - see ADR-0311.
disagreement: The pinned expression tree (ADR-0311) is not correctly rounded: against the exact values it sits 0-22 ULP away on the well-conditioned cases and 228 ULP away on D, where a near-1 root passes through a cancellation. Bit-for-bit agreement with an independent implementation is therefore not achievable, which is what ADR-0311 records and what the `strict` flag below marks.

assertions.bit_for_bit: every case must reproduce `lower` and `upper` exactly, against the pinned tree
assertions.strict_cases: cases with strict:true reproduce the EXACT derivation bit-for-bit, so they are the only values known to be reproducible by any correct implementation
assertions.tolerance_note: TWO bands, because ULP is the wrong measure near zero. The DECISION-relevant question is whether the bound crosses effect_floor, so the absolute band (1e-15) is the primary assertion and applies to every case. The ULP band (64) is a tighter secondary check that catches a real formula error on the well-conditioned cases; cases whose arithmetic passes through a near-0 or near-1 cancellation carry their own `max_ulp` with the reason, because there the two forms provably diverge while remaining the same number to 19 decimal places.

invariants.bounds: 0 <= l <= p <= u <= 1 for every arm, AFTER clamping
invariants.containment: lower <= d <= upper for every case
invariants.within_unit: -1 <= lower and upper <= 1 for every case, by the method itself: U <= u2 - l1 and L >= l2 - u1 by the triangle inequality. Nothing clamps the difference; a clamp would hide a formula error, which is how the first pairing (whose upper reached 2.03 on case G) survived.

cases.note: the realistic case: a ~2pp lift at n~1900 per arm. The bound clears 0, narrowly.
a 10-point lift at n=100 per arm: the bound is negative, so no verdict. The first pairing put it at -0.0118; the method puts it at -0.0155.
zero successes in BOTH arms. The pinned form returns l=0 exactly; the p-form returns a NEGATIVE probability (-2.16e-19), which is why the form is pinned.

all successes in BOTH arms. The exact values are the mirror of C, but the pinned double is not: the upper Wilson root lands a hair either side of 1 and the (u - p) cancellation amplifies that into 228 ULP near 0.0027.
cases.max_ulp_reason: x=n in BOTH arms. The upper Wilson root lands either side of 1 depending on rounding, and that 2 ULP at ~1.0 is amplified through the (u-p) cancellation into 228 ULP at ~0.0027. The ABSOLUTE difference from the exact value is 9.9e-17.

cases.note: small n, huge effect: d 0.8 at n=10 per arm, and the lower bound is 0.45 -- the width small n buys.
identical proportions: d is exactly +0 (not -0) and LOWER must be negative

n=1 knife-edge: one failure against one success. The bound is NEGATIVE (-0.033): one unit per arm can never carry a verdict. The first pairing put this bound at 0.9999999999999999, a verdict on two units.
a tiny effect at large n - the case a floor is supposed to refuse. LOWER is negative, so no verdict.
